title: He heard God’s voice.
paragraphs: Because that means… you can be spiritually gifted—and still be spiritually drifting.

Balaam wasn’t clueless.
He wasn’t pagan in the way we imagine.
He heard God. God spoke to him. God answered him.
And if you’re honest… you’ve felt that tension too.

You know what God said.
But you’re still entertaining what He warned you about.

You pray… but you don’t fully obey.
You worship… but you won’t fully surrender.
You hear conviction… but you delay repentance.
But Scripture doesn’t call it that.
It calls it a divided heart.

In , Balaam stands exposed—not because he lacked revelation, but because he loved reward more than righteousness.
2 Peter 2:15 says he “loved the wages of wickedness.”
Not ignorance.
That’s the part we don’t preach.
You can know truth… and still crave what destroys you.
You can carry a gift… and still negotiate with sin.
You can look anointed… and still be inwardly compromised.
So let me ask you something that might sting a little:
What are you still entertaining… that God already told you to leave?
What voice are you obeying when obedience becomes inconvenient?
Because here’s the tension Balaam teaches us:

God may speak to you…
but that doesn’t mean He has your heart.

The greatest danger is not hearing God incorrectly…
it’s hearing Him clearly and choosing differently.

And compromise doesn’t always look rebellious.
Sometimes it looks spiritual.
Balaam kept going back to God as if maybe the answer would change.

“Lord, are You sure?”
“Maybe this time it’s different…”
“Maybe You’ll allow it now…”
Delayed obedience dressed up as spiritual persistence.
But God is not negotiating truth.
Numbers 23:19 reminds us, “God is not a man, that He should lie… or change His mind.”
So if He already said no…
why are you still walking toward it?
This is where it gets uncomfortable.

Because Balaam couldn’t curse Israel externally…
so he found a way to corrupt them internally (Numbers 25).
He couldn’t attack God’s people head-on…
And some scholars interpret that Balaam advised seduction and idolatry as a strategy when direct opposition failed.
What you don’t conquer, you will eventually start to justify.
And what you justify… will reshape you.

You’re not struggling because God is silent.
You’re struggling because His voice is clear—and costly.

That relationship.
That habit.
That hidden conversation.
That quiet pride nobody sees.
Because obedience will cost you something your flesh still wants.
In Matthew 7:22–23, He says many will prophesy, cast out demons, do mighty works…
God is not impressed with what you can do for Him if your heart refuses to belong to Him.
Because we’ve built a culture that celebrates visibility more than holiness.
Now here’s where grace walks in.
Because this is not just a warning.
If you see Balaam in you—even a little—that’s not condemnation.
Because God is showing you before it destroys you.
And the Gospel meets you there.
Romans 5:8 says, “While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
He didn’t just expose your compromise.
At the cross, your hidden negotiations with sin were not ignored…
And through repentance—real, honest, costly repentance—you don’t just get forgiven.
2 Corinthians 5:17 says if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.
That means you are not destined to live divided.
You are called to live surrendered.

You are not a slave to secret compromise.
You are a son or daughter called into truth and freedom.
And freedom doesn’t come from managing sin.
It comes from surrendering to Jesus.
What do you need to lay down today?

Not tomorrow.
Not when it’s easier.
Now.
Because partial obedience is still disobedience.
And if someone came to your mind while reading this…
And next time… we’re going deeper into the moment Balaam almost obeyed—but didn’t. That tension might expose more than you’re ready for.
